data.gender_notes: Hammel is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Greek word hammon, meaning 'reverence' or 'glory'. In the New Testament, Hammel is a variation of the name Hammonius, who was a shepherd in the Parable of the Good Shepherd. The name Hammel carries the meaning “Honor or Glory” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Hammel usually hope their child will grow to embody honor or glory and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that signifies reverence and honor for the divine.
data.etymology: Hammel belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Honor or Glory.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hammel total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Hammel holds significance in the Christian faith due to its connection with the Parable of the Good Shepherd. In this parable, Jesus describes himself as the good shepherd who lays down his life for his sheep. Hammel, as a name derived from the Greek word hammon or 'reverence', carries the echoes of this doctrine in its etymology. Historically, the name Hammel may have also been associated with the traditional role of shepherds in raising and caring for livestock, connecting it to the agrarian roots of ancient communities.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Hammel holds deep spiritual significance as a reminder of the selfless love and care embodied in the Parable of the Good Shepherd. As a spiritual name, Hammel calls to mind the protective, nurturing role that God plays in our lives, watching over us and guiding us in the same way that a good shepherd watches over his flock. This name serves as a reminder of the divine reverence due to the Creator and the tender, loving care He extends to his children.
